@@@ page: agent
---
title: "How the agent works"
summary: "How the agent writes to you, asks you questions, plans, and gets a second opinion."
order: 11
group: "Using Luxe"
---

## How it writes

The agent is told to keep its replies short and direct, in every mode:

- The answer first, then the reason, then any caveats
- No filler, and no narrating tool calls you can already see
- Plain words over jargon, casual and quick to read
- One question at a time, with a recommended option
- Finished work in a couple of lines: what changed, what was checked, what is left

It is also told to be honest about what it knows. A guess is labeled as a guess, and "I don't know"
is a complete answer. It never says something passed that it did not run, and corrects a wrong
answer as soon as it notices.

When it changes code, it reads what the change touches first, then reaches for the simplest thing
that works: what is already in the codebase, then the standard library, then a platform feature,
then a dependency the project already has. It leaves the work uncommitted unless you ask for a
commit. A command that is yours to run, such as `sudo`, it gives you in a code block to run in your
own terminal.

None of this is a setting. To change how it talks to you, say so ("go more technical with me"), or
put it in your project's [`AGENTS.md`](project-context.md) to make it stick.

## Questions

When the agent needs a decision, it asks in a picker. Each option has a one-line reason, the one it
recommends is marked and selected, so agreeing is one keypress. The last option is always
**Type your own answer**: start typing anywhere and it's picked, so `enter` sends what you wrote.

![A question from the agent, with its recommended answer selected](images/agent-question.svg)

Number keys pick an option, and in a question with one answer they send it. Your answer stays in
the conversation as a card, like the one above the picker. In runs with nobody to answer, such as
`--headless`, the agent takes the default it named, or else its recommended option.

## Plan, then build

A session is in one of two modes, named in the composer's title and in the dock's **MODEL**
section:

| Mode | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **build** | Changes files and runs commands. The default. |
| **plan** | Reads, searches and asks, and writes only `PLAN.md` |

Switch with `shift+tab`, by clicking either, or with `/mode plan` and `/mode build`.
`luxe --plan` starts in plan mode. In plan mode the composer, and the questions the agent asks
there, take a second color.

Plan mode is held in code, not asked for. An edit to any other file, a shell command or a test run
is refused before it runs, and the agent is told why. Switching changes neither the system prompt
nor the tools, so it does not re-read the conversation at full price.

In plan mode the agent asks its open questions one at a time, then writes the plan as one
`## Phase N` section per phase, numbered from 0, which is the shape [`luxe loop`](loop.md) works
through. When a turn writes the plan, Luxe asks what next:

- **Build it here**, with the planning conversation still in context
- **Build it in a fresh session**, starting from `PLAN.md` alone
- **Run it as a loop**: switch to build and say how to start [`luxe loop`](loop.md), which works
  phase by phase with your checks and a review at each
- **Keep planning**

To plan into other files, or on a stronger model:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{
  "plan": {
    "files": ["PLAN.md", "docs/design/*.md"],
    "model": "anthropic/claude-opus-5",
    "thinking": "high"
  }
}
```

The first plain file in `files` is where the plan goes. A model of its own costs something:
each model keeps its own prompt cache, so entering plan mode on another model reads the whole
conversation again at full price. `--model` or `LUXE_MODEL` wins over `plan.model`, and
`--thinking` over `plan.thinking`.

To start every session in plan mode:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "agent": { "default_mode": "plan" } }
```

## A second opinion

`/review` has a reviewer read the uncommitted changes, new files included, in a fresh context: a separate session that
never sees this conversation and changes nothing. Add what to look at hardest:
`/review error handling`. What it would fix goes to the agent as its next turn, and the agent may
push back on a finding it thinks is wrong. A clean review is only shown.

The reviewer runs on your session's model unless you name another. A fresh context is most of what
makes a review useful; another vendor's model adds a second set of blind spots, for a second bill.

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "reviewer": { "model": "openai/gpt-5.6", "thinking": "high" } }
```

The same reviewer is the second check in [`luxe loop`](loop.md#check-each-phase).

## Which model a session starts on

In order, the first that is set:

1. `--model` and `--thinking` on the command line
2. `LUXE_MODEL` and `LUXE_PROVIDER` in the environment
3. The model you last chose
4. `default_model` in `models.json`

Luxe never picks a model for you. With none of these set, sending a message opens the model picker,
and `--headless` and the loop refuse to start. To always start from your configured default rather
than your last choice:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "agent": { "remember_model": false } }
```

## Turn limits

A turn runs until the agent stops calling tools or you stop it with `ctrl+esc`. To cap the rounds
of tool calls in one turn, where calls the model makes together count as one round:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "agent": { "max_tool_iterations": 200 } }
```

At the cap, the agent gets one last reply with no tools, to summarize what it did and what is left.
`LUXE_MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS` sets the cap for one run, and `0` lifts it.

Every setting on this page goes in `~/.config/luxe/config.json`, or a project's `.luxe/config.json`.
`/reload` applies a change without restarting, except to `images`.

## Themes

`/theme` previews each theme as you move through the list. `enter` keeps one and saves it to your
config; `esc` puts back the theme you had.

Luxe's own theme is `luxe`, a warm graphite with a brass accent. Every accent clears a 4.5:1
contrast ratio against the background, and body text 7:1. The others are dark versions of
community favorites and of Omarchy's themes:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Luxe | `luxe` |
| Editors | `jetbrains` (Darcula), `vscode` (Visual Studio 2017 Dark), `xcode` (Default Dark) |
| Community | `aura`, `ayu`, `catppuccin`, `dracula`, `everforest`, `github` (Dark Dimmed), `gruvbox`, `kanagawa`, `monokai`, `noctis-bordo`, `nord`, `one-dark`, `panda`, `rose-pine`, `tokyo-night`, `vesper`, `zenburn` |
| Omarchy | `ethereal`, `hackerman`, `last-horizon`, `lumon`, `matte-black`, `miasma`, `osaka-jade`, `retro-82`, `ristretto`, `solitude`, `vantablack` |

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "theme": "nord" }
```

An unknown name falls back to `luxe`, and Luxe says so when the session opens. See them all on
[luxe.dev](https://luxe.dev/#craft).

Code is colored by the theme too: in answers, tool cards, diffs and the preview, keywords take the
theme's `accentSecondary`, strings its `success`, numbers its `warning`, functions its `accent`,
types its `info`, and comments and punctuation its `muted`. Markdown wears the colors it does in an
answer. A theme of your own, or your Omarchy theme, colors code with no extra setup, and the
website's code blocks are colored the same way.

### Change a few colors

`colors` overrides single colors on top of any theme. A value is `#rrggbb`, an ANSI color number
(`0` to `255`), or `""` for the terminal's own default.

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{
  "colors": {
    "accent": "#7aa2f7",
    "diffAddBg": "#12331f",
    "diffDelBg": "#3a1620"
  }
}
```

The names are the ones a theme file uses; [`luxe.json`](https://github.com/evanwhittaker/luxe/blob/HEAD/crates/luxe-core/src/themes/luxe.json)
lists every one.

One more name is optional: `modePlan`, the color [plan mode](agent.md#plan-then-build) wears on the
composer and the menus and questions around it. Without it, Luxe picks the first of the theme's
other colors that reads as different from its accent.

### Make a theme

A theme is a JSON file in `~/.config/luxe/themes/`, named for the file: `themes/harbor.json` is
`"theme": "harbor"`, and it appears in `/theme` with the built-ins. Its `colors` need only what it
changes; everything else comes from `luxe`. `vars` names colors for the rest of the file to use.

```json title="~/.config/luxe/themes/harbor.json"
{
  "vars": { "harbor": "#2f7d8c" },
  "colors": { "accent": "harbor", "borderAccent": "harbor" }
}
```

This is also how to have a light theme. Start from a copy of
[`luxe.json`](https://github.com/evanwhittaker/luxe/blob/HEAD/crates/luxe-core/src/themes/luxe.json)
for a complete one.

### On Omarchy

Leave `theme` unset, or set it to `omarchy`, and Luxe wears your desktop's theme and changes with
it, within a couple of seconds, in a running session. It uses, in order:

1. A `luxe.json` in the current Omarchy theme. To give every theme one, write a template at
   `~/.config/omarchy/themed/luxe.json.tpl` and Omarchy renders it from each theme's colors.
2. Luxe's built-in theme of the same name, when both are dark.
3. A theme made on the spot from the Omarchy theme's `colors.toml`, with text lifted until it is
   readable. This is how a light Omarchy theme comes out.

A theme you choose with `/theme` stays, whatever the desktop does, unless you choose `omarchy`.
`/theme` saves to your own config, so a theme a project's `.luxe/config.json` sets still wins in
that project.

## Statusline

The statusline is the bar under the composer. Its modules are listed in the order they are drawn:
the left half from the edge inward, the right half from the middle outward.

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{
  "statusline": {
    "visibility": "auto",
    "style": "slab",
    "left": ["project", "branch", "pr", "todo", "changes"],
    "right": ["context", "cost", "tokens", "thinking", "model"],
    "thinking_colors": false
  }
}
```

Those are the defaults. Reorder a list to move modules, and leave one out to hide it. `project`,
`branch`, `pr`, `todo`, `changes`, `cwd` and `activity` belong on the left, the rest on the right,
and a module listed on the other side is not drawn. While auto-approve is on, an `auto-approve`
badge sits on the right whatever the list says.

| Module | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| `project` | The project's name |
| `branch` | The Git branch, with `*` when there are uncommitted changes |
| `pr` | The branch's pull request: `#138 · 1 failing · 2 threads`. Shown only when there is one. |
| `todo` | The agent's checklist: `4/9 · Refine the workspace overview` |
| `changes` | How many files changed, and the key for the [preview](interface.md#preview). Click it to open. |
| `cwd` | The current directory, shortened |
| `activity` | What the turn is doing, and for how long |
| `context` | How full the context window is. Yellow past 75%, red past 90%. |
| `cost` | What the session has cost, or on a subscription, what is left of the plan |
| `tokens` | Tokens sent and received, and the input read from the cache |
| `thinking` | The thinking level |
| `model` | The model, or `no model` until you choose one |

| Key | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `visibility` | `auto` (shown when the dock is not beside the conversation), `shown`, `hidden` |
| `style` | `slab` (each module on its own block) or `flat` (plain text). The dock's headings follow it. |
| `thinking_colors` | `true` colors the thinking level from muted (off) to magenta (ultra) |

When the bar runs out of room, it drops modules in this order: `cwd`, `tokens`, `activity`, `cost`,
`todo`, `changes`, `pr`, `branch`, `project`, then `context` and `thinking`. The model goes last.

## Icons and fonts

`glyphs` sets which icons Luxe draws. Every icon has a word beside it, so nothing is lost at any
setting.

| `glyphs` | Draws | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | `nerd` when Luxe can confirm your font has every icon, otherwise `unicode` | |
| `nerd` | Nerd Font icons | A Nerd Font |
| `nerd_wide` | The same icons, each given two cells | A Nerd Font whose icons are drawn wide |
| `unicode` | Plain shapes: `■ ► ▪ ○ ●` | UTF-8 |
| `ascii` | Plain punctuation: `/ + ~ = x` | UTF-8, for the rest of the screen |

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "glyphs": "nerd" }
```

`auto` asks fontconfig (`fc-list`) whether your fonts have every icon, and picks `nerd` in kitty,
which brings its own. On macOS and Windows without fontconfig, it picks `unicode`; set `nerd` if you
have a Nerd Font. If icons sit flush against the word beside them, you have the wide build of your Nerd
Font: switch to its `Mono` build (see [Fonts](install.md#fonts)), or set `nerd_wide`.

Fonts that draw every character Luxe uses, measured against the font files:

| Font | Missing | Width |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JetBrains Mono | `ℹ︎ ↳︎ ↺︎ ⏸︎ ✔︎ ✖︎`, filled in by your system | 0.60 em |
| IosevkaTerm | nothing | 0.50 em |
| Adwaita Mono | nothing | 0.60 em |
| Monaspace | `⏎︎`, used only by `luxe wire` | 0.62 em |

Use IosevkaTerm's **Term** build: plain Iosevka lets some symbols overlap the next character.

## The conversation

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{
  "conversation": {
    "alignment": "full",
    "growth": "bottom",
    "thinking": "shown",
    "tool_runs": "fold",
    "stream_reveal": "smooth",
    "activity_bar": "bars"
  }
}
```

| Key | Default | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alignment` | `full` | `full` uses the whole width. `left` or `center` cap the width at `prose_max_width` for text and `wide_block_max_width` for code and tables. |
| `prose_max_width` | `120` | 72 to 120 columns, for `left` and `center` |
| `wide_block_max_width` | `140` | 72 to 140 columns, for `left` and `center` |
| `growth` | `bottom` | `bottom` grows up from the composer, like a chat. `top` grows down from the top. |
| `thinking` | `shown` | How the model's reasoning appears: `shown`, `collapsed` to one line, or `hidden` |
| `tool_runs` | `fold` | `fold` draws a run of lookups as one line. `cards` gives each call a card. |
| `tool_details` | `errors` | Which tool cards start open: `errors`, `all` or `collapsed` |
| `stream_reveal` | `smooth` | `smooth` paces streaming text evenly. `off` draws text as soon as it comes in. |
| `activity_bar` | `bars` | The running-turn indicator: `bars`, `dots` or `off` |
| `scroll_lines` | `3` | Lines per mouse wheel notch, 1 to 20 |
| `image_max_rows` | `24` | The tallest an image is drawn, 3 to 200 rows |

## Diffs

Tool cards, the preview and Guided Review draw diffs the same way:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "diff": { "layout": "auto", "word_wrap": false } }
```

| `layout` | Side by side when each column fits |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | 44 columns of code |
| `split` | 28 columns |
| `unified` | Never |

`ctrl+b` switches the preview or Guided Review for the session. A change that only adds or only
removes lines is always one column. Within a changed line, the words that changed are bold.

`word_wrap` wraps long lines in Guided Review instead of scrolling sideways, and `w` switches it
there. Tool cards always wrap, and the preview starts wrapped; `alt+w` switches it.

## Images

Screenshots and images the agent reads are drawn in the conversation where the terminal can:

| `images` | Draws | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | `pixels` in kitty and Ghostty, `off` elsewhere and inside tmux or screen | |
| `pixels` | The picture | A terminal with the kitty graphics protocol |
| `blocks` | A rough preview in colored blocks | Any terminal with color |
| `off` | A line naming the image, with `open ↗` to view it | |

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "images": "auto" }
```

Double-click an image, or select its message (`alt+k`) and press `alt+i`, to view it full-window.
`/images` says which setting is in effect and why. A change to `images` applies the next time Luxe
starts.

## The start screen

The start screen's logotype is drawn in your theme's accent, with a slow shine across it.
`"banner_animation": false` holds it still. See [The start screen](interface.md#the-start-screen)
for its styles, and for skipping it.

`luxe` with no command opens the interface. `luxe --help`, and `--help` after any command, prints
the same reference. `luxe --version` prints the version.

## Starting a session

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `-c`, `--continue` | Resume the most recent session in this project |
| `--resume <id>` | Resume a session by ID; see `luxe sessions list` |
| `--from-pr <number>` | Resume the session that worked on a pull request |
| `--issue <number>` | Start on a GitHub issue, in a worktree of its own |
| `--pr <number>` | Check out a pull request in a worktree and start a session there |
| `--worktree [<branch>]` | Work in a worktree of its own, on a new or named branch |
| `--plan` | Start in [plan mode](agent.md#plan-then-build): read, ask, and write only the plan |

See [Git and GitHub](github.md) and [Sessions and context](sessions.md).

## Model

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--model <id>` | The model, as an ID or `provider/id`, which also picks the provider |
| `--provider <id>` | The provider |
| `--thinking <level>` | `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `ultra`. An unknown level is ignored with a warning. |
| `--api-key <key>` | The key, or `$VAR`, or `!command`. A key typed here is visible to other users of the machine, so prefer the other two. |
| `--base-url <url>` | The endpoint, including its version, such as `/v1` |

These win over the environment and your config for this run only. See
[Models and providers](providers.md).

## Permissions and tools

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--permission-mode <mode>` | `default`, `strict`, `read-only` or `yolo` |
| `--read-only` | The same as `--permission-mode read-only` |
| `--yolo` | Allow everything, with the guardrails off |
| `--auto-approve` | Start with every prompt approved. Interface and `--rpc` only. |
| `--on-ask <allow\|deny>` | What a prompt becomes with nobody to answer: `allow` by default. Headless and loop only. |
| `--trust-project` | Let a project's hooks, permission rules and servers apply |
| `--no-tool <name>` | Turn a tool off for this run |
| `--with-tool <name>` | Turn on a tool your config turned off |

An unknown `--permission-mode` stops the run with an error. It never falls back to a
more permissive mode.

See [Security and permissions](security.md) and [Tools](tools.md).

## Without the interface

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--headless` | Run one prompt and exit |
| `-p`, `--prompt <text>` | The prompt, for `--headless` |
| `--format <text\|json>` | `text` streams the reply to stdout and tool activity to stderr. `json` writes one event per line, with token usage. |
| `--rpc` | Speak the [RPC protocol](rpc.md) on stdin and stdout |
| `--github-writes` | Let an `--rpc` client publish to GitHub: comments, reviews, thread answers, and opening, merging or restacking pull requests. Refused under `--read-only`. |

```bash
luxe --headless -p "list the TODO comments in src/" --format text
```

A headless run needs `-p` and a model: `--model`, `LUXE_MODEL`, your last choice or `default_model`
in `models.json`. It refuses to start without either. It exits with status 1 when the turn fails or Luxe stops before the turn ends, so a
script can tell a failure from an answer without reading the output.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `luxe auth login [provider]` | Sign in. `--method api-key` or `subscription` when a provider has both, `--stdin` to read a key from a pipe, `--api-key <key>` to store one given here, `--no-verify` to skip checking it. |
| `luxe auth list` | Every provider and how it is configured |
| `luxe auth status [provider]` | A credential's type, where it came from, and when it expires |
| `luxe auth logout <provider>` | Remove a stored credential |
| `luxe models list` | Models you can use. `--provider <id>` filters, `--configured` lists only the models `models.json` or `auth.json` names. |
| `luxe models show <provider/id>` | What Luxe knows about a model, and where each value came from. A bare ID uses the active provider. |
| `luxe models refresh` | Refresh the model catalog. `--force` even if it is fresh. |
| `luxe sessions list` | Sessions in this project, newest first |
| `luxe mcp list` | Configured MCP servers |
| `luxe mcp add --id <id> --name <name>` | Add a server to the project's `.luxe/mcp.json`, with `--command "<program> <args>"` or `--url <url>`. It counts as a [project's server](mcp.md#servers-a-project-brings). |
| `luxe mcp remove --id <id>` | Remove a server from the project's `.luxe/mcp.json` |
| `luxe mcp tools` | Every server's tools |
| `luxe mcp login --id <id>` | Sign in to a server, in a browser |
| `luxe loop start` | Start or continue an [autonomous run](loop.md). `--max-turns`, `--compact-percent`, `--pause-percent`, `--quiet`. |
| `luxe loop status` | The run's iteration, phase and cost |
| `luxe loop pause`, `luxe loop resume`, `luxe loop stop` | Pause, clear a pause, or stop the run |
| `luxe loop phase` | The current phase. `--set <n>` changes it. |
| `luxe loop fresh` | Reset the run's turn count; see [Autonomous runs](loop.md#start-a-run) |
| `luxe docs [page]` | Read this guide, offline and for the installed version. `--search <words>` finds lines across every page. |
| `luxe doctor` | Check which tools, language servers and debug adapters work |
| `luxe update` | Update Luxe with the command for however it was installed; see [Updates](configuration.md#updates). `--check` only reports. |
| `luxe init` | Set up a theme, a provider, the tools and the start screen, and write them to `~/.config/luxe/config.json`. `--defaults` skips the questions, `--force` starts from an empty file; see [Editing](configuration.md#editing). |
| `luxe wire <log>` | Summarize a `LUXE_WIRE_LOG` capture; see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#see-what-is-sent-to-the-model). `--tools` breaks the tool schemas' size down per tool. |

Every command also takes the model and permission flags above.

## Command Palette and slash commands

Every command is in two places:

- **Command Palette** (`ctrl+k`) opens over whatever you are doing, anywhere, with your draft left
  where it was.
- **Slash commands**: type `/` at the start of an empty composer and the same commands open above
  it.

![The Command Palette, with the commands used last at the top](images/commands-palette.svg)

Both list only what can run where you are, with the five you used last at the top. Type to filter
by name, slash command or a few words each is known by: `exit` finds **Quit**. A pane beside the
list says what the command does and the arguments it takes.

`enter` runs a command. In the slash list, `tab` puts it in the composer so you can add arguments:
`/diff pr 142`, `/dock left`, `/compact the API decisions`.

Past the command, the list shows the arguments it takes, such as `/diff turn` or
`/diff pr <number or URL>`, and narrows as you type. `tab` fills in the one under the cursor.
`enter` runs it when nothing is missing, and fills it in when it still needs a value. `esc` puts the
list away for that command. In the composer, a command Luxe knows is highlighted, and so are the
words of it you have typed, like `pr` in `/diff pr 142`. A command that stays plain is misspelled.

## Slash commands

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `/help` | Every key for this screen, as you have bound them |
| `/model` | Change the model; the session carries on |
| `/thinking` | How hard the model reasons, from Off to Ultra |
| `/mode` | Switch between build and [plan mode](agent.md#plan-then-build): `/mode`, `/mode plan`, `/mode build` (`shift+tab`) |
| `/review` | A [second opinion](agent.md#a-second-opinion) on the uncommitted changes: `/review`, `/review error handling` |
| `/new` | Start a new session. The current one is kept. |
| `/sessions` | Find another session in this project and pick it up; see [Sessions](sessions.md) |
| `/context` | What fills the context window, largest first |
| `/compact` | Summarize the conversation now. Add what to keep: `/compact the API decisions`. |
| `/cost` | What this session has cost, by model and kind of token |
| `/search` | Find text in the conversation |
| `/diff` | Open a [Guided Review](guided-review.md): `/diff`, `/diff turn`, `/diff base main`, `/diff commit <sha>`, `/diff pr 142` |
| `/preview` | [Preview](interface.md#preview) a file, whole or as its diff: `/preview`, `/preview src/app.rs` |
| `/editor` | Open the project in your editor, or a file: `/editor`, `/editor src/app.rs`, `/editor src/app.rs:42` |
| `/pr` | This branch's pull request: status, reviewers and conversation |
| `/github` | Pull requests and issues on GitHub |
| `/stack` | Restack a stack of pull requests |
| `/worktree` | Where this session works. `/worktree remove` ends it and removes its worktree. |
| `/dock` | Show or hide the dock: `show`, `hide`, `auto`, `left`, `right` |
| `/statusline` | Show or hide the statusline: `show`, `hide`, `auto` |
| `/theme` | Preview and choose a theme |
| `/mouse` | Mouse capture `on` or `off` |
| `/images` | What this terminal can draw, and why |
| `/permissions` | Approve every tool call that would ask you: `on`, `off`. Deny rules still apply. |
| `/tools` | Every tool the agent can use this run, and the ones it cannot |
| `/lsp` | Language servers: which started, and what they are doing |
| `/debug` | Debug adapters, and whether each can be reached |
| `/mcp` | MCP servers, and the tools each offers |
| `/config` | Providers, credentials, settings and config files |
| `/settings` | [Settings](configuration.md#settings) as controls: appearance, the conversation, the dock, tools and the agent |
| `/login`, `/logout` | Add or remove a provider's credential |
| `/auth` | Which providers you are signed in to, and how |
| `/reload` | Re-read your config and keys without restarting |
| `/quit` | Leave Luxe. The session is already saved. |
| `/update` | Leave Luxe and update it, as `luxe update` does |

The Command Palette also lists commands with no slash form, such as **Copy message**, **Swap the
sidebar's side** and, in a review, **Send comments**.

## Help

**Help** (`/help`) shows every key for the screen you are on, grouped and drawn from your own
bindings. In Guided Review it shows the review's keys. Help has no default key, because the obvious
ones do not reach a terminal program reliably. To give it one:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/keybindings.json"
{ "tui.app.toggle_help": ["f1"] }
```

## Default keys

The name in the last column is what `keybindings.json` uses.

**Compose**

| Key | Does | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enter` | Send, or steer a running turn | |
| `shift+enter` | New line | `tui.editor.new_line` |
| `alt+q` | Queue the message for the next turn | `tui.editor.queue_message` |
| `alt+↑` | Bring waiting messages back | `tui.editor.dequeue_message` |
| `ctrl+esc` | Stop the turn | `tui.editor.cancel` |
| `ctrl+v`, `shift+insert` | Paste | `tui.editor.paste` |
| `alt+a` | Select the whole draft | `tui.editor.select_all` |

`enter` and `alt+enter` are fixed. `ctrl+enter` also sends, as `tui.editor.submit`.

**Read**

| Key | Does | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ctrl+↑`, `ctrl+↓` | Scroll | `tui.convo.scroll_up`, `tui.convo.scroll_down` |
| `pageup`, `pagedown` | Scroll a page | `tui.convo.page_up`, `tui.convo.page_down` |
| `ctrl+f` | Search the conversation | `tui.convo.search` |
| `alt+k`, `alt+j` | Select the previous or next message | `tui.convo.select_block_up`, `tui.convo.select_block_down` |
| `ctrl+o` | Full tool output | `tui.convo.toggle_tool_output` |
| `alt+i` | View image | `tui.convo.open_image` |
| `alt+y` | Copy message | `tui.convo.copy_message` |
| `ctrl+insert`, `ctrl+shift+c` | Copy selection | `tui.convo.copy_selection` |

**Conversation**

| Key | Does | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `alt+e` | Edit and resend your last message | `tui.convo.edit_resend` |
| `alt+t` | Ask again | `tui.convo.retry` |
| `alt+g` | Replace the last answer | `tui.convo.regenerate` |

An edit replaces your last message and the answer to it, and **Replace the last answer** drops the
old answer, so the model sees only the new version. **Ask again** sends your last message once
more, after the answer if there was one. The replaced messages stay in the session file but leave
the conversation. All three wait for a running turn to finish.

**Workspace**

| Key | Does | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ctrl+k` | Command Palette | `tui.app.open_palette` |
| `shift+tab` | Switch between build and plan mode, from the composer or the start screen | `tui.app.cycle_mode` |
| `alt+d` | Show or hide the dock | `tui.workspace.toggle_dock` |
| `alt+s` | Show or hide the statusline | `tui.statusline.toggle` |
| `ctrl+p` | Preview | `tui.preview.toggle` |
| `alt+n`, `alt+p` | Next or previous changed file, in the preview | `tui.preview.file_next`, `tui.preview.file_prev` |
| `alt+w` | Wrap long lines, in the preview | `tui.preview.toggle_word_wrap` |
| `alt+o` | Open the file in your editor, in the preview | `tui.preview.open_in_editor` |
| `alt+m` | Show a changed file whole, or its diff, in the preview | `tui.preview.toggle_view` |
| `alt+l` | Ask about the lines you picked, in the preview | `tui.preview.ask_about_selection` |
| `ctrl+t` | Move the keyboard into the dock's file tree, then into the file showing | `tui.workspace.focus_files` |
| `ctrl+g` | Guided Review | `tui.review.open` |
| `ctrl+shift+r` | Reload config and keys | `tui.app.reload` |
| `ctrl+c` | Quit | `tui.app.quit` |

**Guided Review**

| Key | Does | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `c` | Comment on this line | `tui.review.add_finding` |
| `a` | Ask the agent | `tui.review.ask` |
| `alt+enter` | Finish review | `tui.review.finish` |
| `alt+u` | Send comments | `tui.review.send` |
| `alt+c` | All comments | `tui.review.findings` |
| `e` | Edit the selected comment | `tui.review.edit_finding` |
| `x` | Delete the selected unsent comment | `tui.review.delete_finding` |
| `r` | Resolve or reopen the selected comment | `tui.review.resolve_finding` |
| `alt+r` | Reanchor the selected stale comment | `tui.review.reanchor_finding` |
| `]`, `[` | Next or previous chapter | `tui.review.chapter_next`, `tui.review.chapter_prev` |
| `n`, `shift+n` | Next or previous hunk | `tui.review.hunk_next`, `tui.review.hunk_prev` |
| `enter` | Open what the cursor is on | `tui.review.open_selection` |
| `home` | Back to column zero | `tui.review.line_start` |
| `g`, `alt+v` | Show or hide the guide | `tui.review.toggle_guide` |
| `f` | Open or fold collapsed churn | `tui.review.toggle_noise` |
| `ctrl+b` | Side by side, or one column | `tui.review.toggle_split` |
| `w` | Wrap long lines | `tui.review.toggle_word_wrap` |
| `s` | Change what is reviewed | `tui.review.source` |
| `ctrl+r` | Refresh the review | `tui.review.refresh` |
| `o` | Open on GitHub | `tui.review.open_in_browser` |
| `shift+e` | Open the file in your editor, at the cursor's line | `tui.review.open_in_editor` |
| `alt+←` | Back to the conversation | `tui.review.return_chat` |
| `?` | Help | `tui.review.help` |

## Rebind keys

Put your bindings in `~/.config/luxe/keybindings.json`, or open it from **Configuration** with
**Edit configuration files**. Each entry is a name from the tables above and a list of keys:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/keybindings.json"
{
  "tui.app.open_palette": ["ctrl+p"],
  "tui.preview.toggle": ["alt+p"],
  "tui.app.toggle_help": ["f1"]
}
```

- A binding replaces that action's default keys rather than adding to them.
- A key you bind is taken from any action that had it by default.
- A key is modifiers and one key joined by `+`: `ctrl`, `shift`, `alt`, then a letter, a digit,
  `enter`, `esc`, `tab`, `space`, `backspace`, `delete`, `insert`, an arrow (`up`, `down`, `left`,
  `right`), `home`, `end`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, or `f1` to `f12`.
- An unknown name or key is skipped with a warning in the log, and the rest still load. An action
  whose keys are all invalid is left with none, rather than its defaults.
- A project's `.luxe/keybindings.json` applies over yours.

`/reload` or `ctrl+shift+r` applies a change without restarting.

## Alt keys on a Mac

A Mac has no Alt key. Its Option key types characters instead: `option+o` is `ø`, `option+p` is
`π`. Most of Luxe's `alt` keys need your terminal to send Option as Alt:

| Terminal | Setting |
| --- | --- |
| Ghostty | `macos-option-as-alt = true` (or `left`) |
| iTerm2 | **Profiles › Keys › Left Option key: Esc+** |
| Terminal | **Settings › Profiles › Keyboard › Use Option as Meta key** |
| kitty | `macos_option_as_alt yes` |
| WezTerm | Left Option already sends Alt; for the right one, `send_composed_key_when_right_alt_is_pressed = false` |
| Alacritty | `option_as_alt = "Both"` under `[window]` |

Ghostty already does this on the "U.S." keyboard layouts. On the others it sends the character and
marks it as an Alt key. On "ABC", the Mac's default English layout, Luxe reads that back as the key
you pressed, so `option+o` opens a file from the preview without any setting. On other layouts, set
the option above.
@@@ page: configuration
---
title: "Configuration"
summary: "Where Luxe's files live, what a project can set, and every key in config.json."
order: 1
group: "Customize"
---

Luxe works with no configuration. Everything here is optional, and most of it can be set from inside
Luxe: **Configuration** (on the start screen, or `/config`) signs you in and opens these files in
your editor, [`/settings`](#settings) changes the settings you use most, `/theme` sets the theme,
and `/model` the model.

## Files

Your own files live in `~/.config/luxe/` (`%APPDATA%\luxe` on Windows). A project can have its own
in `.luxe/` at its root.

| File | Holds | In a project |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config.json` | Appearance, behavior, and the settings on this page | `.luxe/config.json`, over yours |
| `keybindings.json` | Your keys; see [Commands and keys](commands.md#rebind-keys) | `.luxe/keybindings.json`, over yours |
| `models.json` | Model and provider settings; see [Custom providers](custom-providers.md) | |
| `auth.json` | Credentials; see [Models and providers](providers.md#where-credentials-are-kept) | |
| `permissions.json` | What the agent may do; see [Security](security.md) | `.luxe/permissions.json`, which can only tighten yours |
| `hooks.json` | Commands run at points in a turn; see [Hooks](hooks.md) | `.luxe/hooks.json`, only with `--trust-project` |
| `mcp.json` | MCP servers; see [MCP](mcp.md) | `.luxe/mcp.json` or `.mcp.json` |
| `lsp-servers.json` | Language servers; see [Tools](tools.md#add-a-language-server) | |
| `debug-adapters.json` | Debug adapters; see [Tools](tools.md#debugger) | |
| `agents.md` | Instructions for every project; see [Project context](project-context.md) | `AGENTS.md` |
| `themes/` | Your own themes; see [Appearance](appearance.md#make-a-theme) | |
| `skills/` | Your own skills; see [Skills](skills.md) | `.luxe/skills/` or `.agents/skills/` |

`LUXE_CONFIG_DIR` moves the whole directory, and every file in it.

### What a project cannot change

A project's `.luxe/config.json` overrides yours key by key, with a few exceptions. These run
programs, reach the network, or decide what a repository is trusted with, so Luxe reads them from
your own config only:

- `launchers` and `mentions`, which run programs
- `update`, and `github.refresh_secs`
- `lsp.project_servers`
- `agent.on_ask`, which a project can set to `deny` but not to `allow`
- `agent.cache_warming`, which a project can turn down but not up, since it spends your money

Project `gate.commands` also run programs. Luxe ignores them and warns unless you start with
`--trust-project`. With trust, a nonempty project list replaces your global list. Otherwise, the
loop uses your global commands. Move the list to your own config if you don't want to trust the
project.

### Editing

`luxe init` asks the first run's questions again (a theme, a provider, the tools, and the start
screen) and writes the answers to `config.json`, changing only those keys. It also writes a
`config.schema.json` beside it so your editor can complete and check every key. `--defaults` writes
a file that chooses nothing, without asking, and so does a run with no terminal; with a
`config.json` already there, either one needs `--force`, which removes the old file first. Luxe ignores a key it does
not know, so an old config always loads on a newer Luxe; check the spelling if a setting seems to
do nothing.

`/reload` (`ctrl+shift+r`) applies changes to `config.json` and `keybindings.json` without
restarting.

## Settings

![The Tools page of the settings](images/configuration-settings.svg)

`/settings`, or **Settings** in **Configuration**, shows the settings you are most likely to change
as controls, on five pages: Appearance, Conversation, Dock & statusline, Tools, and Agent. Each
change writes one key to your `config.json` and leaves the rest of the file as it was.

| To | Key |
| --- | --- |
| Choose a setting | `↑` / `↓` |
| Turn it on or off, or step to the next choice | `space`, `enter` or `→` |
| Step back a choice | `←` |
| Remove it from your file, so the default applies | `r` |
| Open `config.json` in your editor | `e` |
| Search every page | `/` |
| Change page | `tab`, or `1` to `5` |

Each value says where it comes from: `default`, `global` (your `config.json`), or `project` (this
project's `.luxe/config.json`, which wins over yours, so it is changed there). Most settings take
effect at once; the rest say they take effect the next time Luxe starts. That includes the Tools
page, because the tools the agent is offered are fixed for a run. In a window too small for the
panel, it says so instead, and only `esc` works until the window fits.

## Behavior

### Notifications

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "notifications": true, "bell": false }
```

`notifications` sends a desktop notification while the terminal is in the background, when a turn
finishes or fails, a tool call waits for your approval, the agent asks you a question, or a Guided
Review finishes writing its guide. To pick some of those, list them:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "notifications": ["permission", "question"] }
```

| Name | When |
| --- | --- |
| `turn` | A turn finished or failed |
| `permission` | A tool call is waiting for your approval |
| `question` | The agent asked you something |
| `review` | A Guided Review finished writing its guide |

`bell` rings the terminal bell at each of those moments. Both are off by default. Many terminals
turn a bell into a request for the window manager's attention, which can pull focus from what you
are doing.

The notification goes through your terminal, as an escape sequence it turns into a desktop
notification, so it works over ssh and needs nothing installed. Ghostty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm,
Warp and foot show them; Luxe recognizes those and sends nothing to a terminal it does not know. If
yours shows them and Luxe does not recognize it, name the sequence: `"notification_method": "osc9"`
(the common one) or `"osc777"`. Inside tmux, add `set -g allow-passthrough on` to your tmux
configuration. Your terminal may also have to be allowed to send notifications in your system's
settings.

### herdr

Inside a [herdr](https://herdr.dev) pane, Luxe tells herdr whether it is working, idle, or waiting
on you, and why: `Approve bash`, or the question it asked. herdr shows that in its sidebar, raises
its own notification when Luxe finishes or needs you (set in herdr's `[ui.toast]`), and reports it
to `herdr agent wait`. After a herdr restart, the pane reopens the same session with
`luxe --resume`. Luxe sends no escape-sequence notifications inside herdr, because herdr keeps
them for itself.

[Recipes](recipes.md#luxe-colors-in-herdr) has a Luxe palette for herdr's theme.

This is local to your machine and on by default. Outside herdr nothing is sent.
`LUXE_HERDR=0` in the environment stops the reports, and so does the config:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "herdr": false }
```

### Updates

Once a day, Luxe checks whether a newer release exists, and when one does the start screen says
*Update available · /update*. The check sends nothing about you or your machine; the comparison
happens locally.

`/update`, or `luxe update` in a shell, updates Luxe with the command for however you installed
it, showing each one before it runs:

| Installed with | `luxe update` runs |
| --- | --- |
| The install script | `luxe-cli-update`, the updater it put beside `luxe` |
| Homebrew | `brew update`, then `brew upgrade luxe` |
| Cargo | `cargo install --locked --force luxe-cli` |

Luxe never downloads or replaces its own program; whatever installed it does. A copy your system's
package manager owns is left to it, and a downloaded archive points you at the releases page. On
Windows, Luxe can't be replaced while it runs, so it prints the command to run once it has exited.
Afterwards it checks that the `luxe` your shell finds is the new version, and says so if another
copy earlier on your `PATH` is in the way. `luxe update --check` only reports.

To stop the daily check:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "update": { "check": false } }
```

`LUXE_UPDATE_CHECK=0` turns it off as well. `luxe update` still checks when you run it.

### Launchers

A launcher gives a key to a program that takes over the terminal and gives it back, such as gh-dash
or lazygit:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{
  "launchers": [
    { "key": "alt+g", "command": "gh-dash" },
    { "key": "ctrl+alt+l", "command": "lazygit" }
  ]
}
```

Luxe keeps running underneath and redraws when the program exits. Text the program writes to the
file named by `$LUXE_HANDOFF` is put in the composer, so a gh-dash command can send
`#123 look at this` to Luxe. A launcher's key wins over any other binding.

@@@ page: custom-providers
---
title: "Custom providers"
summary: "Connect any endpoint, and set a model's context window, thinking levels, request format and samplers."
order: 6
group: "Extend"
---

Luxe knows how to reach every provider in [Models and providers](providers.md), and the
[models.dev](https://models.dev) catalog tells it each model's context window, output limit,
thinking levels and price. This page is for what neither covers: your own endpoint, a model the
catalog does not know, or a local server that needs its requests shaped a particular way.

Everything here goes in `~/.config/luxe/models.json`. `luxe models show <provider>/<id>` shows what
Luxe resolved for a model, and where each value came from.

## Add an endpoint

**Connect a local or custom model** in **Configuration** asks for an endpoint and writes it here.
By hand:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/models.json"
{
  "providers": {
    "gateway": {
      "base_url": "https://llm.internal.example.com/v1",
      "api_key": "$GATEWAY_KEY",
      "api": "openai-completions"
    }
  },
  "models": {
    "gateway/qwen3-coder-480b": { "context_window": 262144, "max_tokens": 65536 }
  }
}
```

Then `luxe --model gateway/qwen3-coder-480b`, or choose it in `/model`.

| Provider key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `base_url` | The endpoint, including its version, such as `/v1` |
| `api_key` | The key: the value, `$VAR`, `${VAR}` or `$env:VAR`, or `!command`, which runs each time a request needs the key. An unset `${VAR}` is empty, as in `mcp.json`, and Luxe logs which one. |
| `api` | The API it speaks: `openai-completions` (the default), `openai-responses`, `anthropic-messages` |
| `auth` | How the key is sent: `bearer`, `x-api-key`, `api-key`, or `foundry` for both of the last two |
| `models_dev` | The models.dev provider to take model details from, when the names differ |
| `compat` | How requests are shaped; see [Request format](#request-format) |
| `sampling_params` | Samplers for every model it serves; see [Samplers](#samplers) |

A provider in `models.json` replaces the same provider's block in `auth.json` whole, so keep a
provider's key and endpoint in one file. A provider Luxe already knows keeps everything you do not
write. A key in a provider Luxe knows is used when its own variable, such as `OPENAI_API_KEY`, is
unset; for one it does not know, the key you write comes first and `OPENAI_API_KEY` is the
fallback. A key you signed in with comes before either.

A file Luxe cannot parse is skipped with a warning in the log, and a misspelled key is ignored, so
check the result with `luxe models show <provider>/<id>` after editing.

## Model settings

Settings for one model go under `models`, by `provider/id`. Each value overrides the catalog's,
and everything you leave out still comes from it. `thinking_level_map`, `modalities` and `cost`
each replace the catalog's whole: a `cost` you write drops the catalog's long-prompt prices, and an
`output` price you leave out is free.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `context_window` | The model's context window, in tokens |
| `max_tokens` | The most it may write in one reply. Defaults to the model's own limit from the catalog. Luxe lowers it per request to what the window has left, so setting the real limit is safe; setting a lower one is how replies get cut off. |
| `name` | The name shown in the picker and statusline |
| `reasoning` | Whether it can think |
| `thinking` | The level a session starts at for this model |
| `thinking_level_map` | What each thinking level sends; see below |
| `modalities` | What it accepts: `["text"]` or `["text", "image"]` |
| `cost` | Prices per million tokens: `input`, `output`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`, and `cache_write_1h` for a write kept for an hour (twice `input` if unset) |
| `compat`, `sampling_params` | Override the provider's, key by key |

A model the catalog does not know gets a 128k context window and no output limit until you set
them. Anthropic endpoints require a limit, so there Luxe asks for 128k. If the model allows less,
Anthropic's refusal names its real limit, and Luxe retries with that and uses it for the rest of the
session.

## Thinking levels

`thinking_level_map` says what each of Luxe's levels sends to the model. `null` marks a level the
model cannot do, removing it from `/thinking`; a level Luxe needs falls back to the nearest one that
is left. `ultra` is the name for a provider's `max`.

```json title="~/.config/luxe/models.json"
{
  "models": {
    "lmstudio/qwen3.8-27b": {
      "reasoning": true,
      "thinking": "medium",
      "thinking_level_map": {
        "off": "none",
        "minimal": null,
        "low": "low",
        "medium": "medium",
        "high": "high",
        "xhigh": "high",
        "ultra": null
      }
    }
  }
}
```

A level you do not map sends its own name, and `off` sends `none`; `xhigh` and `ultra` are offered
only once mapped. Setting a map also marks the model as one that reasons.

An endpoint Luxe does not know sends no thinking setting at all until its `compat` says how: for
most OpenAI-compatible servers, `"thinking_format": "openai"`, which sends `reasoning_effort` on
every request, `off` included. See [Request format](#request-format).

For Anthropic models, Luxe uses adaptive thinking with an effort level where the model supports
it, and a token budget for older ones. If a model refuses how thinking was requested, Luxe tries
the other way once and remembers it for the session. `compat.force_adaptive_thinking` forces
adaptive thinking for an endpoint the catalog does not know.

## Request format

`compat` says how a request has to be shaped for an endpoint to accept it. On a provider it applies
to every model the provider serves; on a model, only the keys you write override the provider's.

```json title="~/.config/luxe/models.json"
{
  "providers": {
    "lmstudio": {
      "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1",
      "compat": { "supports_developer_role": true, "supports_reasoning_effort": true, "thinking_format": "openai" }
    }
  },
  "models": {
    "lmstudio/qwen3.6-27b-fable-fusion": {
      "compat": { "thinking_format": "chat_template", "supports_developer_role": false }
    }
  }
}
```

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `supports_developer_role` | Send the system prompt as `developer` rather than `system` |
| `supports_reasoning_effort` | Allow `reasoning_effort` to be sent |
| `thinking_format` | How thinking is requested: `openai`, `qwen`, `deepseek`, `openrouter`, `together` or `chat_template` |
| `chat_template_kwargs` | What to send for `chat_template`; see [below](#chat-templates) |
| `max_tokens_field` | `max_tokens` or `max_completion_tokens` |
| `supports_usage_in_streaming` | Ask for token usage while streaming. On by default. |
| `requires_tool_result_name` | Name the tool on each tool result. gpt-oss needs this. |
| `cache_control_format` | How prompt caching is requested: `anthropic` or `openrouter` |
| `force_adaptive_thinking` | Use Anthropic's adaptive thinking |
| `supports_long_cache_retention` | Ask Anthropic to keep cached prompts for an hour rather than five minutes. Each cache write costs 2x input instead of 1.25x. Off by default, since not every Anthropic-compatible endpoint accepts it. |
| `stream_tool_arguments` | Stream a `write` call's file from Anthropic as it is written, so its card fills in live. On by default; turn off for an endpoint that rejects a tool's `eager_input_streaming` field. |
| `defer_tool_loading` | Load a tool the agent asks for with `activate_tools` where it asked, so the cached prompt stays cached. On by default. Luxe stops on its own for an endpoint that refuses it; turn it off for one that accepts it and then misbehaves. Anthropic and Responses endpoints only. |
| `copilot_headers`, `openrouter_headers` | Send those services' identifying headers. With `copilot_headers`, each model also goes to the Copilot endpoint it takes. |
| `use_responses_api` | Use OpenAI's Responses API. Provider only; prefer `"api": "openai-responses"`. |

`anthropic-messages` endpoints read only `force_adaptive_thinking`, `cache_control_format`,
`supports_long_cache_retention`, `stream_tool_arguments`, `defer_tool_loading` and
`copilot_headers`. The rest are for
OpenAI-style endpoints. `luxe models show` lists any flag that differs from the
provider's.

## Samplers

A local model's card often gives a sampling recipe with settings the OpenAI format has no field for,
such as `top_k`, `min_p` and `repeat_penalty`. `sampling_params` is added to the request as written,
after Luxe's own fields, so its values win:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/models.json"
{
  "models": {
    "lmstudio/qwen3.8-27b": {
      "sampling_params": { "temperature": 1.0, "top_p": 0.95, "top_k": 20, "min_p": 0.0 }
    }
  },
  "providers": {
    "lmstudio": { "sampling_params": { "min_p": 0.0 } }
  }
}
```

A provider's samplers apply to every model it serves, and a model's override them one key at a
time. Nothing is checked, so an unknown key goes to your server as is; `model`, `messages`, `input`,
`stream` and `tools` are refused. OpenAI-style endpoints only.

## Chat templates

A server that renders the model's chat template, such as `llama-server`, takes thinking settings as
`chat_template_kwargs`. Each template names them differently, so you describe them:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/models.json"
{
  "providers": {
    "llama-server": {
      "base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1",
      "compat": {
        "thinking_format": "chat_template",
        "chat_template_kwargs": {
          "enable_thinking": { "$var": "thinking.enabled" },
          "reasoning_effort": { "$var": "thinking.level", "omit_when_off": true },
          "preserve_thinking": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`thinking.enabled` becomes `true` or `false`, and `thinking.level` the value `thinking_level_map`
gives the current level. `omit_when_off` leaves the key out when thinking is off. Anything else is
sent as written. LM Studio ignores `chat_template_kwargs`; use `"thinking_format": "openai"` there.

## Model details

Luxe takes a model's details from three places, each overriding the one before, value by value:

1. The models.dev catalog built into Luxe, which works offline
2. A fresher copy, refreshed in the background into `~/.cache/luxe/models-dev.json`
3. Your `models.json`

```console
$ luxe models show anthropic/claude-opus-5
anthropic/claude-opus-5
  name              Claude Opus 5  [models.dev]
  context window    1.0M  [models.dev]
  max output        128k  [models.dev]
  reasoning         true  [models.dev]
  thinking levels   high, low, medium, ultra, xhigh  [models.dev]
  thinking control  effort (adaptive thinking), never off  [models.dev]
  modalities        text, image  [models.dev]
  cost /Mtok        $5.00/$25.00  [models.dev]
```

Each value names where it came from: `snapshot` for the catalog built into Luxe, `models.dev` for
the refreshed copy, `config` for your `models.json`, and `default` where none of them said.

| Variable | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `LUXE_MODELS_DEV_REFRESH=0` | Never refresh; the built-in catalog still answers |
| `LUXE_MODELS_DEV_URL` | Refresh from a mirror |
| `LUXE_MODELS_DEV_PATH` | Keep the catalog in this file instead. The refresh writes there too, so pair it with `LUXE_MODELS_DEV_REFRESH=0` to pin a file of your own. |
| `LUXE_MODELS_DEV_TTL` | Seconds between refreshes. 21600 by default. |

## Microsoft Foundry

### Keyless sign-in with Microsoft Entra ID

If your Foundry resource has key sign-in turned off, give Luxe a command that prints a token:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/models.json"
{
  "providers": {
    "foundry-anthropic": {
      "auth": "bearer",
      "api_key": "!az account get-access-token --scope https://ai.azure.com/.default --query accessToken -o tsv"
    },
    "foundry-openai": {
      "api_key": "!az account get-access-token --scope https://ai.azure.com/.default --query accessToken -o tsv"
    }
  }
}
```

Run `az login` first. Only the Claude provider needs `auth`; the others already send a bearer
token. The command runs for each request and nothing is kept, so a token from `az`, which lasts
about an hour, is replaced as it expires and a long session carries on.

### Choose which deployments Luxe offers

Luxe records what a resource has deployed in each provider's `served_models`, and the model behind
any deployment named something else in `deployments`, which is where it looks up the context window
and price. If your key cannot list deployments, or you want to choose the list yourself, turn
discovery off and write both:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/models.json"
{
  "providers": {
    "foundry-anthropic": {
      "discover_deployments": false,
      "served_models": ["sonnet-prod", "claude-opus-5"],
      "deployments": { "sonnet-prod": "claude-sonnet-5" }
    }
  }
}
```

`discover_deployments: false` on any of the three providers stops Luxe asking the resource at all.

### Thinking on partner models

`foundry-completions` sends no thinking setting by default, because its models disagree on how to
take one. Turn it on per model:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/models.json"
{
  "models": {
    "foundry-completions/deepseek-v4-flash": {
      "compat": { "supports_reasoning_effort": true },
      "thinking_level_map": { "high": "high", "ultra": "max" }
    }
  }
}
```

Use `reasoning_effort` only: Foundry refuses DeepSeek's own `thinking` format. Foundry does not
report these models' thinking tokens, so `/cost` counts them as output.

A Foundry deployment can have a different context window and price from the vendor's own API.
Luxe uses Azure's figures for Foundry models.

## OpenRouter

- Luxe asks OpenRouter to cache prompts for Claude models, which it otherwise does not, and which
  makes later turns of a session far cheaper. `"cache_control_format": null` in the provider's
  `compat` stops it.
- Some models on OpenRouter cannot turn thinking off. For those, Luxe leaves the setting out and
  the model thinks at its own default. `luxe models show openrouter/<id>` says `never off`.
- Luxe identifies itself to OpenRouter with its `HTTP-Referer` and `X-Title` headers, which carry
  nothing about you. `"openrouter_headers": false` in `compat` drops them.
@@@ page: environment
---
title: "Environment variables"
summary: "The environment variables you can set, and the ones Luxe sets."
order: 3
group: "Reference"
---

An environment variable wins over the same setting in a config file, and a command-line flag wins
over both. A variable that turns something off, such as `LUXE_HERDR=0`, cannot turn back on what a
config file turned off.

## Model and provider

| Variable | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LUXE_MODEL` | | The model, as an ID or `provider/id` |
| `LUXE_PROVIDER` | | The provider |
| `LUXE_API_KEY` | | A key for the provider the session starts on |
| `LUXE_BASE_URL` | | That provider's endpoint, including its version |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, … | | Each provider's own key; see [Models and providers](providers.md#providers) |
| `LUXE_STREAM_START_TIMEOUT` | `60` | Seconds to wait for a reply to start. `0` waits forever. |
| `LUXE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT` | `180` | Seconds a reply may go quiet. `0` waits forever. |
| `LUXE_PROVIDER_RETRIES` | `3` | Tries after the first when a provider fails before answering |
| `LUXE_COPILOT_PLAN_USAGE` | `1` | `0` stops reading how much of your GitHub Copilot plan is used |

## Files

| Variable | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `LUXE_CONFIG_DIR` | Where configuration and credentials live, instead of `~/.config/luxe` |
| `LUXE_STATE_DIR` | Where Luxe keeps its state, such as the model you last chose, MCP sign-ins and the logs of commands that only report, instead of `~/.local/state/luxe` |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` | Honored on every platform; see [Install](install.md#where-luxe-keeps-files) |

When Luxe works out where its files go, a path in one of these, or in `HOME`, that is not valid
UTF-8 is ignored, as if the variable were unset.

## Model catalog

| Variable | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LUXE_MODELS_DEV_REFRESH` | | `0` never refreshes, and the built-in catalog still works. `1` refreshes at every start. Unset refreshes once the copy is older than `LUXE_MODELS_DEV_TTL`. |
| `LUXE_MODELS_DEV_URL` | `https://models.dev/api.json` | Refresh from a mirror, as a full URL |
| `LUXE_MODELS_DEV_PATH` | | Keep the catalog in this file. The refresh writes there too, so pair it with `LUXE_MODELS_DEV_REFRESH=0` to pin a file of your own. |
| `LUXE_MODELS_DEV_TTL` | `21600` | Seconds between refreshes |

## Tools and turns

| Variable | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LUXE_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECS` | | Replace the time limit of every tool that has one |
| `LUXE_MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS` | | Most rounds of tool calls in one turn. `0` lifts a configured cap. |
| `LUXE_COMPRESS` | `1` | `0` stops trimming long command output, though output past the size limit is still cut |
| `LUXE_LSP_ON_EDIT` | `1` | `0` stops adding language server errors, and notes about missing tests, after edits |
| `LUXE_SIZE_CHECK` | `1` | `0` stops telling the agent when an edit takes a file past 500 lines or a function past 20 |
| `LUXE_DEBUG_NUDGE` | `1` | `0` stops suggesting the debugger after repeated test failures |
| `LUXE_PLAN_NUDGE` | `1` | `0` stops reminding the agent to update its checklist |
| `LUXE_LAZY_TOOLS` | `1` | `0` sends every tool's description with every request |
| `LUXE_CORE_TOOLS` | | The tools sent with every request, comma-separated; the rest load when needed |
| `LUXE_DAP_STOP_TIMEOUT_SECS` | `30` | How long the debugger waits for a program to stop |
| `LUXE_MAX_DEPTH` | `2` | How deeply Luxe may run inside itself, as with [subagents](recipes.md#subagents) |
| `LUXE_WEB_ALLOW_PRIVATE` | | `1` lets `web_fetch` and `screenshot` reach your local network and files |
| `LUXE_WEB_TIMEOUT_SECS` | `30` | How long one fetch may take. Past 60, raise `LUXE_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECS` too. |
| `BRAVE_API_KEY`, `TAVILY_API_KEY`, `EXA_API_KEY`, `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` | | Search providers, and Firecrawl for pages built with JavaScript; see [Tools](tools.md#web) |

## Integrations

| Variable | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `LUXE_EDITOR`, then `VISUAL`, then `EDITOR` | The editor Luxe opens files in |
| `LUXE_FILE_MANAGER`, then `FILE_MANAGER` | The file manager `O` in the dock's file tree opens a folder in. Without either, the first of yazi, lf, ranger and nnn that is installed, then your desktop's own. |
| `LUXE_HERDR` | `0` stops reporting state to [Herdr](recipes.md#run-luxe-in-herdr) |
| `LUXE_UPDATE_CHECK` | `0` turns off the update check |

## Diagnostics

| Variable | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `LUXE_LOG` | What goes in the log, such as `debug` or `luxe_core=debug`. `RUST_LOG` works too. See [Logs](troubleshooting.md#logs). |
| `LUXE_WIRE_LOG` | A file to record every request sent to the model; see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#see-what-is-sent-to-the-model) |

## Set by Luxe

| Variable | Is |
| --- | --- |
| `LUXE_DEPTH` | How deeply this run is nested inside another Luxe |
| `LUXE_REVIEW_GATE_ACTIVE` | Set for a loop's [gate commands](loop.md#check-each-phase), so a Luxe they start does not run a gate of its own |
| `LUXE_HANDOFF` | For a [launcher](configuration.md#launchers): a file whose contents go in the composer when the program exits |
@@@ page: extending
---
title: "Extending Luxe"
summary: "Which kind of extension you need, how to install one, and what stays stable across updates."
order: 1
group: "Extend"
---

Luxe extends through files and programs, never through code loaded into Luxe itself. A file carries
instructions or settings; a program carries behavior, and runs with the same access you have.
Installing an extension is copying a file.

## Which one you need

| To | Use | Runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Change how Luxe looks, or which tools exist | [Configuration](configuration.md) and [themes](appearance.md#make-a-theme) | Nothing |
| Teach the agent a procedure or house style | [Skills](skills.md) and [`AGENTS.md`](project-context.md) | Nothing |
| Point the agent at your tracker or runbooks with `@` | [Mention sources](mention-sources.md) | Your program, when its tab opens |
| Give the agent new tools | [An MCP server](mcp.md) | Your program, when the agent calls it |
| Block, rewrite, audit or react to what the agent does | [Hooks](hooks.md) | Your program, at points in a turn |
| Use an endpoint or model Luxe does not know | [Custom providers](custom-providers.md) | Nothing, or your `!command` for a key |
| Drive Luxe from your own program, or build a new front end: conversation, Guided Review and GitHub | [The RPC protocol](rpc.md) | Your program, driving Luxe |
| Open another terminal tool with a key | [Launchers](configuration.md#launchers) | Your program, on a key |

The rows are in order of effort; the first that fits is usually right. [Recipes](recipes.md) puts
several together: Asana in the `@` picker, subagents, a classifier guard, running in Herdr, and a
local model in LM Studio.

## Where extensions live

```text
~/.config/luxe/
├── config.json           settings, launchers, mention sources
├── keybindings.json      keys
├── models.json           endpoints and models
├── permissions.json      what the agent may do
├── agents.md             instructions for every project
├── skills/
│   └── <name>/           a skill
├── hooks.json            hooks
├── mcp.json              MCP servers
├── themes/
│   └── <name>.json       a theme
├── lsp-servers.json      language servers
└── debug-adapters.json   debug adapters

<project>/
├── .agents/skills/       skills committed with the repository
├── .mcp.json             MCP servers
└── .luxe/
    ├── config.json       settings, less what a project cannot change
    ├── keybindings.json
    ├── skills/
    │   └── <name>/
    ├── mcp.json
    ├── hooks.json        only with --trust-project
    └── permissions.json  can only tighten yours, unless --trust-project
```

What a project's `config.json` cannot change is listed in
[Configuration](configuration.md#what-a-project-cannot-change). On Windows, your own folder is
`%APPDATA%\luxe`, and `LUXE_CONFIG_DIR` moves it anywhere. These paths do not change between
releases.

`.luxe/` writes its own `.gitignore`, which keeps everything in it out of Git except
`permissions.json`, `mcp.json`, `hooks.json` and `skills/`. To share more with your team, such as the
project's `config.json`, write that `.gitignore` yourself: Luxe rewrites its own copy, but leaves
alone one it did not write.

## Trust

**A repository does not choose what runs on your machine.** Its hooks and its loop
`gate.commands` run only with `--trust-project`, and its permission rules can only make yours
stricter. MCP servers, language servers and formatters it brings start, by default, only in an
interactive session or with `--trust-project`; `lsp.project_servers` in your own config changes
that, see [Tools](tools.md#a-server-the-project-installed). This is about which programs Luxe starts. A
language server itself may run project code, as rust-analyzer does with `build.rs`, so open an
unfamiliar repository in Luxe the way you would build it.

**A repository can still write instructions.** Its `AGENTS.md` and skills reach the model. Luxe
removes text a reviewer cannot see, but plain text is still instructions, so read an unfamiliar
repository's `AGENTS.md` as you would its `Makefile`.

## What stays stable across updates

| | Across updates |
| --- | --- |
| `config.json`, `models.json`, `keybindings.json`, `lsp-servers.json`, `debug-adapters.json` | **Only added to.** An old file always loads. An unknown key is ignored, and no key changes meaning. |
| Sessions in `.luxe/sessions/` | A newer Luxe reads every older session. An older Luxe skips what it does not know in a newer one. |
| The RPC protocol | Adding to it changes nothing. Removing or renaming anything changes `protocol_version`. |
| Hook points | Added, never renamed. An unknown point skips that hook alone, with a warning in the log. |
| Tool arguments | A renamed argument still accepts its old name. |
| Skills and `AGENTS.md` | Plain markdown |
| The paths above | Do not move |

Before 1.0, a minor release may change the RPC protocol and the hook points, and its release notes
will say so. Config files and sessions keep the stronger promise regardless, since they are the two
you cannot regenerate.

## What Luxe will not add

- **Plugins loaded into Luxe.** A plugin would have all of Luxe's access, however it was sandboxed.
- **A network listener for RPC.** It would turn a local program into a service that needs
  authentication.
@@@ page: github
---
title: "Git and GitHub"
summary: "Worktrees, issues, opening and merging pull requests, review threads, and stacks."
order: 7
group: "Using Luxe"
---

Everything that talks to GitHub goes through the GitHub CLI, `gh`, signed in with your own account
(`gh auth login`). Without it, the rest of Luxe works and these features say why they cannot.

## Work in a worktree

```bash
luxe --worktree                # a new branch, luxe/session-…
luxe --worktree fix-the-loop   # a branch you name
```

The session gets its own Git worktree under `.luxe/worktrees/`, on a new branch made from
`origin`'s default branch, fetched first, or from your current commit when the remote is not
`origin` or `origin/HEAD` was never set. A branch you name that already exists is checked out as it
is. The agent works there, so you can keep working in your own checkout and
your uncommitted changes are never touched. `.luxe/` keeps its own contents out of Git, so the
worktree stays out of `git status`.

- `/worktree` says where the session is working.
- `/worktree remove` ends the session and removes the worktree, once everything in it is committed.
  The branch stays.
- Resuming the session goes back into its worktree, and recreates it from the branch if it was
  removed.
- `"worktree": { "always": true }` in `config.json` gives every new session one.

## Start from an issue

```bash
luxe --issue 123
```

Luxe reads issue #123, makes a worktree on a branch named for it (`123-short-title`), and starts a
session there. The issue and its latest comments go to the agent with your first message, so "fix
it" is enough. They are treated as the reporter's words to weigh, not as instructions.

`enter` on an issue in `/github` does the same. If one of your sessions already took the issue up,
it resumes that session instead.

## Fix a pull request

```bash
luxe --pr 142        # check it out in a worktree and start a session
luxe --from-pr 142   # resume the session already working on it
```

A plain `git push` from the worktree updates the pull request, including one from a fork. A fork's
branch that has to be renamed here, such as its `main` checked out as `mara/main`, gets a remote of
its own (`mara-push-main`) for that push, so pushes from the fork's other branches are not
redirected. Luxe refuses a pull request that is merged or closed, that your account cannot push to,
or whose author turned off edits by maintainers.

## Open a pull request

Review the work with [Guided Review](guided-review.md), finish (`alt+enter`), and choose **Open pull
request**. Luxe drafts the title and description from the review, with `Closes #123` when the
session started from an issue.

![The pull request, drafted from the review](images/quickstart-pull-request.svg)

The heading says where it merges and what happens first, such as `commits and pushes first`.
Nothing happens until you press `enter`.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `t` | Edit the title |
| `e` | Edit the description |
| `E` | Edit the description in your editor (`$LUXE_EDITOR`, `$VISUAL` or `$EDITOR`) |
| `d` | Open it as a draft |
| `enter` | Open it |

Afterward, `o` opens it in the browser, and the session remembers it for `luxe --from-pr`.

## Browse GitHub

`/github` lists this repository's pull requests and issues, with the one under the cursor shown
beside the list. Each tab is a GitHub search:

| Tab | Lists |
| --- | --- |
| **Review requested** | Open pull requests waiting on your review |
| **Mine** | Your open pull requests |
| **Assigned issues** | Open issues assigned to you |
| **Pull requests** | Every open pull request, most recently updated first |
| **Issues** | Every open issue, most recently updated first |

It opens on the first tab with something in it.

![/github, with a pull request's overview](images/github-overview.svg)

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `tab`, `shift+tab` | Next or previous tab |
| `/` | Edit the tab's search |
| `s` | Show open, closed, merged, or all |
| `x` | Put the tab's own search back |
| `→` / `←` | Into the detail and back |
| `pagedown` / `pageup`, `home` / `end` | Move ten rows, or to either end |
| `enter` | Review the pull request, or start a session on the issue |
| `c` | [Mention](mentions.md) it in the composer |
| `o` | Open it on GitHub |
| `r` | Read it all again from GitHub |
| `esc` | Close `/github` |

### Search

The line above the rows shows the tab's search. Press `/` to edit it, then `enter` to run the tab
again with your search. Use the same syntax as GitHub's search box: `is:merged`, `label:bug`,
`author:mara`, `sort:created-asc`. While you type, plain words narrow the rows already loaded, so
you can see a match before you search for it.

![Editing a search in /github](images/github-search.svg)

A changed tab is marked with `*` and keeps your search until you close Luxe. `x` puts back the
tab's own search, and so does running an empty search.

The tabs always stay in this repository. A `repo:`, `org:` or `user:` you type is ignored.

A tab loads 30 rows at a time and shows how many there are in all, as in `30 of 214`. Moving to the
last row loads the next 30.

### Your own tabs

To list other searches, replace the tabs. `{repo}` stands for this repository. A tab without it
searches all of GitHub, and so does any search you type in it:

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{
  "github": {
    "sections": [
      { "name": "Needs review", "query": "is:open is:pr label:needs-review repo:{repo}" },
      { "name": "Everywhere", "query": "is:open is:pr review-requested:@me archived:false" }
    ]
  }
}
```

A project's `.luxe/config.json` can set its own sections.

## Your pull request

The dock and the statusline show the current branch's pull request: `#138 · 1 failing · 2 threads`.
`/pr` opens it. Its **Overview** lists what stands between it and merging, and each row that can be
dealt with here has a key:

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `f` | **Fix with agent**: write a request naming the failing checks into the composer, for you to send |
| `x` | **Resolve conflicts**: the same, for a conflict with the base |
| `t` | **Resolve threads**: open the unresolved review threads in Guided Review |
| `u` | **Update branch** with its base. In a stack, opens `/stack` instead. |
| `R` | **Mark ready** for review |
| `enter` on **Ready** | Merge, after a confirmation |

The merge confirmation offers the methods the repository allows (merge commit, squash, rebase),
starting on the one you used last there; `tab` switches and `d` chooses whether the branch is
deleted. While something still stands in the way, an **Auto-merge** row turns on GitHub's
auto-merge instead. If anything was pushed after you looked, GitHub refuses the merge and the
confirmation says so.

## Answer review threads

1. In `/pr`, press `t`. The unresolved threads open in Guided Review as comments on their lines,
   against your working tree.
2. `alt+u` sends them to the agent. It reads them as the reviewers' words, not as instructions.
3. Verify each fix (`r` in **Feedback**), then commit and push.
4. `alt+enter` and choose **Answer on GitHub**. Threads you verified are resolved; `c` adds a reply
   in your own words.

## Conversation

**Conversation** is the second tab in `/pr` and `/github`: the description, comments, reviews and
threads, oldest first.

![A pull request's conversation, with a drafted reply](images/github-conversation.svg)

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `enter` | Expand or fold a comment |
| `r` | Reply, in the thread or as a new comment quoting what it answers |
| `d` | Have the agent draft the reply. It reads, and changes nothing. |
| `b` | Hide bots |

A reply is written in place. `ctrl+enter` keeps what you wrote, and `esc` while writing drops what
you typed since. A kept reply waits for you: `e` writes in it again, `E` opens it in your editor,
`enter` posts it, and `esc` leaves it under what it answers. Nothing reaches GitHub without that `enter`,
and nothing in the conversation reaches the agent unless you mention it.

## Stacks

When a review has two or more chapters, finishing offers **Open as a stack**: one pull request per
chapter, each based on the one below. The lower ones get branches named `<branch>-part-1`,
`-part-2` and so on, and yours is on top. It needs the reviewed work uncommitted.

When a lower branch changes, `/stack` moves the ones above it back on top. It shows what will move
first, makes the new commits without checking anything out (with `git replay`, Git 2.44 or later),
and stops on a conflict before changing anything. `enter` force-pushes every branch that moves in
one push, each only if GitHub still has what `/stack` read. It refuses, pushing nothing, when a
moving branch here has moved, been checked out or switched, or has uncommitted changes since the
preview. If the push goes through but the branches here cannot follow, it says so.

After the bottom pull request is squash-merged, keep its branch until `/stack` has moved the next
one. Deleting it through the API, with `gh pr merge --delete-branch`, makes GitHub close the pull
requests based on it.

## How often Luxe checks GitHub

Luxe reads the pull request after anything that could change it, such as a push or `/pr`, and on
an interval otherwise: every 15 seconds while checks run, every minute once things settle, and every
five minutes when the terminal has been in the background for a while. Each read costs one point
of the 5,000 an hour your `gh` sign-in allows.

```json title="~/.config/luxe/config.json"
{ "github": { "refresh_secs": 60 } }
```

`refresh_secs` sets the settled interval, and `0` turns the interval off. This one is read from
your own config only, not a project's.
@@@ page: guided-review
---
title: "Guided Review"
summary: "Read a change chapter by chapter, comment for the agent, and finish with a commit, fixes or a pull request."
order: 6
group: "Using Luxe"
---

Guided Review reads a change back to you in the order it makes sense, split into chapters. Each
chapter says what changed, why, and how it was checked, beside the code. Comments you leave go to
the agent as work to do.

![A review: the guide on the left, the hunk being read on the right](images/review-guide.svg)

## Open a review

Press `ctrl+g`, or run `/diff`. Luxe writes the guide first; when `review ready` shows above the
composer, press `ctrl+g` again to open it. Asked for while a turn is running, the review waits for
the turn to end. A review you already have opens at once, and one you had open when Luxe stopped
comes back with your comments.

| Review | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Uncommitted changes | `/diff` |
| What the last turn changed | `/diff turn` |
| Everything since a branch or commit | `/diff base main` |
| One commit | `/diff commit 4c1e2a0` |
| A pull request | `/diff pr 142`, `/diff pr #142`, or its address |

Inside a review, `s` changes what it covers: uncommitted changes, the last turn, a base or a commit.
A pull request takes `/diff pr`. If the agent committed its work, so nothing is uncommitted,
`ctrl+g` and `/diff` review the last turn instead. Luxe remembers what you have already reviewed in
each project, so the next review leads with what is new since then.

## Read it

The guide on the left opens with why the change exists and what it does, then a block per chapter
with its files. The right pane shows the hunk you are on, with the guide's sentence about it. Drag
the line between them to give the guide more or less room; double-click it to go back.

| To | Key |
| --- | --- |
| Next step. Past the last one, finish. | `space` or `n` |
| Previous step | `shift+n` |
| Next or previous chapter | `]` / `[` |
| Next or previous file | `ctrl+↓` / `ctrl+↑` |
| Scroll | `↑` / `↓`, `pageup` / `pagedown`, or half a page with `ctrl+d` / `ctrl+u` |
| Hide the guide, or the hunk's sentence | `g` / `z` |
| Side by side, or one column | `ctrl+b` |
| Wrap long lines | `w` |
| Search | `/` |
| Every key in the review | `?` |
| Back to the conversation | `esc`. The review stays pinned until you return. |

### What needs you

A review lists the hunks that need your attention and accounts for the rest. A hunk covered by a
test that passed says so on its own header and stays in the diff. Lockfiles, generated files,
moves and formatting-only changes fold away, each run of them in a file into one row; `f` opens
them all.

Three things are flagged and stay on the list, whatever else passed. Each flagged file says so on
its row and in the walkthrough, and the guide gives the total for any kind with more than two:

- A line that looks like a credential (`sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `AKIA…`, a `password = "…"`)
- A weakened check: a deleted test, an added `#[ignore]`, an edit to CI or `deny.toml`
- A file the agent edited without reading first

If a test fixture needs a value that looks like a credential, mark that line with
